title: Run state while a pull request is open
intro: Already fixed: the pull request is opened; nothing checks it afterwards. Asked: what a run should show while its pull request waits.

decisions.title: Run state while the pull request is open
decisions.question: While a run's pull request is open, should the run say it is waiting for review until GitHub merges it?
decisions.today: Today the run is marked done in the same step that opens the pull request. Nothing checks that pull request afterwards, so a red check or a merge never changes the run.
decisions.after: With the recommended option, the run shows as waiting for review after its pull request opens. It turns done only after GitHub merges the pull request. A red check sends the run back to the fix stage with the failing output.
decisions.preview:
Today:
  run fix-login   status: done
  pull request #123 is open. Nothing watches it.

After:
  run fix-login   status: awaiting_approval
  Pull request #123 waits for review: https://github.com/example/repo/pull/123

options.name: Wait for review until merged
options.see: After the pull request opens, the run shows as waiting for review. It turns done only after the pull request merges. A red check sends the run back to fix, with the failing output.
options.asks: Nothing new. Merge or close the pull request on GitHub, as you do today.
options.how: The run waits at a review stop. A background pass checks the pull request and starts the run when its state changes. Only the run's own process changes its status.
pros: Matches the spec's status table and its merge review stop, so no spec change is needed
Every status change stays in the process that holds the run's lock
cons: A run whose work is finished shows waiting, not done, until the merge
Needs a new case for a review stop that has no decision file, in the run's code and in the background pass

options.name: Done when the pull request opens
options.see: The run shows done as soon as its pull request opens, as it does today. If a later check goes red, the run reopens and goes back to fix.
options.how: Keep the status as it is now. A background pass looks at done runs that still have an open pull request, and reopens one whose checks turn red.
pros: Smallest change: the run's status stays as it is today
The dashboard keeps showing done for finished work
cons: Done stops meaning finished, and it departs from the spec's status table
Housekeeping treats done as finished (housekeeping.py:28), so cleanup could take a run whose pull request is still open
Reopening a run is a status change from outside its lock holder, or a second route to the same change

options.name: Background pass changes the run
options.see: The run shows done as today. A separate background pass watches its pull request and sends red checks back to fix, without the run's own process.
options.how: The background pass changes the run's status and starts its fix stage, instead of the run's own process doing it.
pros: No change to the run's process or its status table
cons: Breaks the rule that only the process holding a run's lock writes its status
Two places decide what a red check means: the background pass and the run's own rework rules

decisions.why: It is the state the spec already describes, and it keeps every status change inside the process that holds the run's lock.
